data_source: IMF World Economic Outlook via DataMapper (latest vintage, accessed October 2026)
inflation_management: The dirham's peg to the dollar (3.6725 since 1997) anchors UAE monetary policy, and inflation has followed the property-and-oil cycle: 12.3% in 2008 on the pre-crisis boom, deflation of -4.7% in 2009, near zero in the early 2010s, -2.1% in 2020, then 4.8% in 2022, easing to a projected 1.3% in 2025. The 2018 introduction of 5% VAT added a one-off lift. The central bank shadows the Fed; with an open capital account and the peg, domestic demand (notably Dubai property cycles) is the main inflation driver, and it has been well contained.
debt_management: Federal-level debt is low, but the consolidated picture including emirates is what matters: the IMF series shows debt rising from 5.1% of GDP in 2006 to 21.1% in 2009 after the Dubai debt crisis, easing to 13.5% by 2014, then climbing to 35.7% in 2021 on COVID and oil before settling at a projected 34.3% in 2025. Dubai's 2009 standstill on Dubai World debt was restructured without federal bailout. Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth (ADIA, Mubadala) dwarfs all liabilities; net debt is deeply negative. The ratio is a footnote to asset strength.

key_events.event: Dubai debt crisis; Dubai World sought a standstill; Abu Dhabi provided $10bn support.
Oil crash; fiscal consolidation and subsidy cuts began.
COVID-19 and the oil crash; Expo 2020 delayed a year; debt hit 30.1%.
Abraham Accords normalized relations with Israel, opening trade and investment.
Oil windfall; GDP hit $511.4bn and property boomed.
Diversification (tech, finance, tourism) continued; debt projected at 34.3% in 2025.

outlook_next_decade: The UAE's base case is strong: diversification away from oil is the most advanced in the Gulf, sovereign wealth is enormous, and Dubai/Abu Dhabi compete credibly as global hubs. Risks are property-cycle excesses, regional tensions, and the long-run energy transition, though ADNOC's low-cost production cushions it. Fiscal policy is counter-cyclical by Gulf standards. Analytical assessment: one of the region's most resilient economies, with the main question being execution of diversification rather than any macro constraint.
caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
